narratives.Description: bug(agents,bootstrap): both managed AGENTS.md recovery pointers dangle on a fresh clone; #2273 guard misses agents-entry.md
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Both bootstrap-recovery pointers in the managed `AGENTS.md` section name paths that do not exist in a fresh consumer clone. One is circular (it routes recovery into the payload whose absence triggers it); the other names a file `directive init` never deposits. The #2273 guard that was written to prevent exactly this does not cover the carrier the pointers live in.

## The two pointers

Source: `content/templates/agents-entry.md`, rendered into the consumer's managed `AGENTS.md` section.

**1. Circular fallback** (`agents-entry.md:6`):

> `! If any .deft/core/.agents/skills/ path here cannot be read (missing, stale, or a redirect stub), read .deft/core/QUICK-START.md and follow it`

The trigger condition is a `.deft/core/` path being unreadable. The remedy is to read another `.deft/core/` path. `init` adds `.deft/core/` to `.gitignore`, so on a fresh clone the target is guaranteed absent at exactly the moment the line fires.

This also contradicts the rule stated fourteen lines below it in the same file (`agents-entry.md:20`):

> `Bootstrap: cold-start → README § Cold-start (#2273) ⊗ never .deft/core/`

**2. Undeposited target** (the rule above, as rendered into a consumer repo).

`README § Cold-start` refers to the `deft:cold-start-bootstrap v1` block. That block exists only in this repository's own `README.md`. `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts` never writes a `README.md`, so a consumer repo without one has no such block — and a greenfield `directive init` does not create it.

The block's own text asserts a guarantee that is false for every consumer:

> This block is always committed (never gitignored) and does **not** depend on the `.deft/core/` payload being present, so it is reachable on a fresh clone even when the vendored framework is missing.

So the designated safe target is itself unreachable in the repos it was designed to protect.

## Why the #2273 guard did not catch this

`packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/main_md_preamble.test.ts` encodes the rule:

> #2273: the recovery pointer is now payload-INDEPENDENT -- it points at the Cold-start bootstrap block at the top of the committed `README.md`, NOT at `.deft/core/UPGRADING.md` (the exact vendored payload that is absent when recovery is needed).

Two gaps:

1. **Scope.** `CANONICAL_PATHS = ["main.md", "SKILL.md"]`. `content/templates/agents-entry.md` is not covered.
2. **Shape.** The assertion is a single-literal denylist — `expect(head).not.toContain(".deft/core/UPGRADING.md")`. `.deft/core/QUICK-START.md` is a different literal and passes.

Separately, `agents_entry_contract.test.ts` lists `"## Cold-start bootstrap (#2273)"` under `retiredFullTextMarkers`, i.e. the cold-start block was deliberately thinned out of `AGENTS.md` down to a pointer. That left `agents-entry.md:6` as the only bootstrap escape hatch in the carrier, still aimed at the gitignored payload.

The managed section also means a consumer cannot repair either line locally without sha drift against `agents:refresh`.

## Reproduction (v0.116.0)

1. Greenfield repo, `directive init --yes`, commit, clone the branch fresh.
2. In the clone: `.deft/` is absent, `.deft/core/QUICK-START.md` is absent, no `README.md` exists.
3. Resolve every `.deft/core/*` reference in the committed tree — all dangle, including the fallback target.

## Expected

1. Repoint the `agents-entry.md:6` fallback at something guaranteed present in a fresh consumer clone. Options, in preference order:
   - A fileless instruction (`npm i -g @deftai/directive && directive doctor`) — depends on no repo file at all.
   - The README cold-start block, **if** `init` is changed to deposit it (creating `README.md` when absent).
   Do not simply swap `QUICK-START.md` for the README reference; today that trades one dangling target for another.
2. Generalize the #2273 guard from a single-literal denylist to the property it stands for: no bootstrap-recovery pointer in any managed carrier may name a `.deft/core/` path. Extend `CANONICAL_PATHS` to include `content/templates/agents-entry.md`.
3. If the README block is chosen as the target, `init` must deposit it, and a test must assert it survives a fresh clone.

## Related

- #2273 — established payload-independent cold-start recovery; this is the carrier it missed.
- #2065 — managed vs unmanaged `AGENTS.md` header, why the consumer cannot self-repair.
- #4424 — consumer report; the P1 on this fallback is the one finding in that report that is a product bug rather than review scoping.

## Verdict

The refutation target survives. Re-verified at `24867a86`: both pointers do dangle on a greenfield fresh clone, and the #2273 guard does not cover the carrier. I found no way to refute it.

Three blocking findings are against the **Expected remedy**, not the premise. As written, items 1-3 cannot be implemented: the proposed property red-fails the two carriers already under the guard, the proposed `CANONICAL_PATHS` extension breaks three sibling assertions, and the chosen-target option that satisfies item 1 leaves the second pointer defective at three more sites.

**Re-verification method.** `vitest` could not run in the dest (no `node_modules`). I replicated the guard's exact assertions -- first-12-line window, the three `toContain` needles, the `not.toContain` denylist -- with a script over blobs read via `git show 24867a86:<path>`. Results are quoted below, not cited.

---

## blocks-the-design -- Expected 2's property red-fails `main.md` and `SKILL.md` on day one

**Evidence.** Replicating the head-12 window over the pinned blobs:

```
main.md          head names ANY .deft/core/ path : true
SKILL.md         head names ANY .deft/core/ path : true
agents-entry.md  head names ANY .deft/core/ path : true
```

`main.md:3` and `SKILL.md:4` both read "does not depend on the `.deft/core/` payload being present". That is prose *about* the payload, not a pointer at it -- but it is the same substring.

**Failure mode.** Implement "no bootstrap-recovery pointer in any managed carrier may name a `.deft/core/` path" as a head-window denylist and the suite goes red immediately on the two carriers `CANONICAL_PATHS` already holds, for text that is correct. The predictable repair is to carve an exception, and the exception is the hole again.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected 2 cannot bind as stated. The property that actually covers both pointers is *the named recovery target resolves in a fresh consumer clone*, evaluated over resolved targets -- not a path-spelling denylist. See also the `content/UPGRADING.md` finding below, which a `.deft/core/` denylist cannot match at all.

---

## blocks-the-design -- extending `CANONICAL_PATHS` breaks three sibling assertions

**Evidence.** `CANONICAL_PATHS` drives five `it.each` blocks (`main_md_preamble.test.ts:19-45`), not one. Against the pinned `agents-entry.md`:

```
line1 == "<!-- DEFT-PREAMBLE-V1 -->"     : false   (actual: <!-- deft:managed-section v3 -->)
head contains "Cold-start check"         : false
head contains "README.md"                : false
head contains ".deft/core/UPGRADING.md"  : false   <- the denylist that was supposed to fire
```

**Failure mode.** Adding `agents-entry.md` to that list fails `preamble_marker_at_line_one`, `preamble_includes_gate_instruction` and `preamble_references_cold_start_recovery` -- three failures that have nothing to do with #2273 -- while the one assertion the issue wants still passes.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected 2 must name a *separate* carrier list scoped to the payload-independence assertion, not reuse `CANONICAL_PATHS`. Secondary: the spelling. `resolveRepoPath` probes `content/<rel>` first and falls back to repo root (`helpers.ts:19-29`), so the layout-agnostic spelling is `templates/agents-entry.md` -- the convention `agents_entry_contract.test.ts:792` already uses. `content/templates/agents-entry.md` resolves in the source repo only by fallback and does not survive the C1 flatten.

---

## blocks-the-design -- option A satisfies item 1 while leaving pointer 2 defective at three sites

**Evidence.** The README pointer is not only at `agents-entry.md:20`. `main.md:3` and `SKILL.md:4` carry it verbatim, including the guarantee the issue correctly identifies as false:

> read the **Cold-start bootstrap** block at the top of the project's `README.md` ... `README.md` is always committed (never gitignored) and does not depend on the `.deft/core/` payload

**Failure mode.** Expected 1 offers two options; Expected 3 is conditional on option B being chosen. Take option A (fileless) and the issue closes with `agents-entry.md:6` repaired, `agents-entry.md:20` / `main.md:3` / `SKILL.md:4` still naming a block no consumer repo has, and no proposed test firing on any of them.

**Honest scoping.** `main.md` and `SKILL.md` deposit into `.deft/core/` (content-manifest C1), so on a *fresh* clone they are absent and their pointer is moot. The live case is the other two-thirds of `agents-entry.md:6`'s own trigger -- "stale, or a redirect stub" -- where the payload is present, the pointer fires, and the target does not exist.

**Disposition consequence.** Either make Expected 3 unconditional, or make Expected 1 repoint all four sites. The current Expected can be fully satisfied with the defect intact.

---

## sharpens-framing -- a registered recovery ladder already exists; Expected 1 proposes a fourth spelling

**Inventory.** `packages/core/src/doctor/constants.ts:19-23` -- "One recovery ladder for doctor FAIL `suggested_fix` (#4090). One spelling per rung":

```
RECOVERY_LADDER_AGENTS_REFRESH = "deft agents:refresh"
RECOVERY_LADDER_UPDATE         = "deft update"
RECOVERY_LADDER_NPX_PREFIX     = "npx @deftai/directive"
RECOVERY_LADDER_NPM_GLOBAL     = "npm i -g @deftai/directive"
```

More directly: `checkQuickStartResolves` (`doctor/checks.ts:495-525`) **is** the "does the recovery target resolve" check, aimed at `<installRoot>/QUICK-START.md`, and its fail path hands back the fileless ladder. `recovery_ladder.test.ts:98-127` pins those spellings and asserts the fail detail never names `.deft/core/run`.

**Failure mode.** Expected 1's literal `npm i -g @deftai/directive && directive doctor` is a new spelling in a carrier nothing pins. `recovery_ladder.test.ts` holds the registered rungs; the template string drifts alone, and #4090's one-spelling invariant is quietly broken by the fix for #4430.

**Disposition consequence.** State the remedy as *reuse the #4090 ladder constant* and extend the one-spelling assertion to cover the managed carrier. Do not mint a template literal.

---

## sharpens-framing -- depositing the README block verbatim reintroduces a payload-dependent recovery link

**Evidence.** The only link inside the `deft:cold-start-bootstrap v1` block (`README.md:1-14`) is at rung 5:

```
](./content/UPGRADING.md#corporate-or-mirrored-npm-registry)
```

`content/` flattens to `.deft/core/` in a consumer deposit (content-manifest C1 LOCATION INVARIANT). `README.md:16`, just below the block, has the same shape (`./content/docs/SUPPORT.md`).

**Failure mode.** Expected 3 deposits the block; the E404 / ETARGET mirror rung -- a recovery rung, inside the block whose stated purpose is payload independence -- points into the gitignored payload. Worse for the guard: the committed spelling is `content/UPGRADING.md`, which `not.toContain(".deft/core/UPGRADING.md")` does not match, so the #2273 assertion stays green over a reintroduced payload-dependent recovery link.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected 3 must say *deposit a rewritten block whose every rung is fileless or repo-root-committed*, and this case is the reason the Expected-2 property has to resolve targets rather than match path spellings.

---

## sharpens-framing -- "guaranteed absent" is greenfield-only

**Evidence.** `init-deposit/gitignore.ts:25,32` -- `.deft/core/` is the "greenfield only per Option B / #1941 split" line; `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` deliberately excludes it. `gitignore.test.ts:195` and `:214` pin "does not add `.deft/core` to gitignore when the deposit is already tracked."

**Failure mode.** The Summary's "`init` adds `.deft/core/` to `.gitignore`, so on a fresh clone the target is guaranteed absent" holds for the greenfield repro and not for a tracked/hybrid-committed deposit. The risk is an acceptance test written as "assert the target is absent after a fresh clone", which passes greenfield and is vacuous on a tracked deposit.

**Disposition consequence.** Scope the claim to greenfield / untracked deposits, and state that the fix must hold on both -- the pointer must resolve whether or not the payload happens to be committed.

---

## Injection / swarm lens -- fires (managed prompt surface, attacker-influenced trigger)

Not N/A: the target is the managed `AGENTS.md` section -- an always-loaded agent prompt that, per #2065, a consumer cannot repair locally without sha drift against `agents:refresh`.

**Evidence.** `agents-entry.md:6`'s trigger is "missing, stale, or a **redirect stub**" -- a *file-absence or file-content* condition, writable by anything with the checkout: a stale `deft update`, a sibling worktree, a PR that deletes a skill file, a planted stub.

**Failure mode.** Today that trigger fails closed: the target dangles, the agent stops or asks. Expected 1 option A replaces it with an unconditional "install a global npm package and run it", so deleting or stubbing any `.deft/core/.agents/skills/*` path reliably drives an unpinned `npm i -g` in every subsequent agent session, from a prompt line the consumer cannot edit. This is a swarm amplifier: N dispatched subagents all read the same managed section.

**Deterministic control (not reviewer attention).** The README ladder already carries both mitigations and Expected 1's one-liner drops both -- rung 1 is "Already installed? Run `directive doctor`" before any install, and the block preamble fixes the version: "the version to install is always the one pinned in the project's committed `package.json`". If option A is chosen, the carrier line must be doctor-first and pinned, sourced from the #4090 constant so `recovery_ladder.test.ts` holds its shape.

**Disposition consequence.** Option A is not strictly safer than option B; it trades a dangling target for an absence-triggered install. That trade belongs in the Expected preference order, which currently ranks A first on "depends on no repo file at all" alone.

---

## footnote -- the retired marker's recorded canonical home is `commands.md`, not README

`agents_entry_contract.test.ts:512-526` lists `"## Cold-start bootstrap (#2273)"` under `retiredFullTextMarkers` for spec `session-routing-2493`, whose `canonicalHome` is `commands.md` -- i.e. `.deft/core/commands.md`. The issue's reading (thinned down to a pointer) is right about the thinning; the destination recorded in the test is a third target, itself payload-resident. Worth one line in whatever replaces the guard, so the relocation record and the pointer agree.

## footnote -- recording obligations

Stop 1 write-back (`5640576934`) carries the model/role lead, the clearance line, `mechanism-shaped: true`, `arc-mode: no-ingest`, `yolo-standing`, dest, `origin-ref`, `dispatch-sha`, charter, spend + why, `refutation-target`, target, target-shape, audit-targets. Round-1 ceiling is the write-back, as the contract requires. `N=1`, so no panel-deposit is owed. Nothing to flag.

---

## Road not taken

I considered proposing a new committed-surface registry -- enumerate every path named in a managed carrier, resolve each against the post-init committed tree. Rejected: the content-manifest already classifies which entries flatten into `.deft/core/`, so target resolvability is derivable from existing data, and `checkQuickStartResolves` already supplies the check shape. A new registry would be a second source of truth for the same fact. What would flip this: if the manifest records only the *shippable* set and not the post-init *committed* set, the derivation does not close and a registry is warranted.

## Steelman of the position I am arguing against

The strongest case for the Expected as written: the single-literal denylist is a two-line fix, adding `.deft/core/QUICK-START.md` and the carrier path is cheap, and it is green today. Shipping that beats designing a resolvability property nobody has budget for.

It fails on pointer 2. `README § Cold-start` contains no `.deft/core/` literal at all, and the deposited-block variant would spell its dangling link `content/UPGRADING.md`. A literal denylist cannot reach the harder half of the bug, and shipping it records the bug as fixed.

What would flip me: change `init` to deposit a *rewritten* cold-start block whose every rung is fileless or repo-root-committed. Then every remaining recovery target is committed by construction, and a path-spelling denylist plus a deposit-survives-fresh-clone test is genuinely sufficient. That is Expected option B done unconditionally -- which is the disposition I would take.

## Bound remedy

- Replace Expected 2's path-spelling denylist with a resolvability property: the named recovery target must resolve in a fresh consumer clone. Do not reuse CANONICAL_PATHS; add a separate carrier list for that assertion. Use the layout-agnostic spelling `templates/agents-entry.md`.
- Expected 1 reuses the #4090 recovery-ladder constants (`RECOVERY_LADDER_*` in doctor/constants.ts), doctor-first then pinned install. Do not mint a new template literal. Extend the one-spelling assertion to the managed carrier.
- Make Expected 3 unconditional, or make Expected 1 repoint all four sites (agents-entry.md:6, agents-entry.md:20, main.md:3, SKILL.md:4). If a README cold-start block is deposited, rewrite every rung so it is fileless or repo-root-committed; do not copy `./content/UPGRADING.md`.
- Scope "guaranteed absent" to greenfield / untracked deposits. The pointer must resolve whether or not the payload happens to be committed.
- Option A is an absence-triggered global install from a consumer-unrepairable prompt. Rank it with that trade, not as strictly safer than depositing a rewritten committed block.
